name: Rosario
source: Instituto Nacional del Agua (INA) alert system a5 API; Prefectura Naval Argentina gauges
datum: m above the local gauge zero (cero de escala); INA lists the zero at 2.923 m IGN (Argentine national vertical datum)
license: INA alert system (alerta.ina.gob.ar); data from Prefectura Naval Argentina gauges. No license is stated on the API or site. Credit INA and Prefectura Naval Argentina; clear reuse terms before publishing.
notes: INA series 34 ('medición directa', variable 'Altura hidrométrica'), station Rosario (INA station 34, PNA code 280), owner PNA.
INA publishes no per-value quality flag, so every value is marked measured. This includes the most recent days, which INA may still correct.
53738 raw observations. Days with more than one reading (averaged to a daily mean): 1285, from 2016-01-04 to 2026-07-10. Before that each day has a single reading.
INA alert thresholds for this gauge: alert 5 m, evacuation 5.25 m, low water 1.64 m.

measurement_history.fact: INA/UTN report: the Rosario gauge has records from 1884.
INA metadata: Prefectura staff gauge (not automatic), zero at 2.923 m IGN.

Antico et al. (2020) digitized typewritten daily Rosario levels for 1875 to 1883, tied them to the modern datum and corrected them for errors from a gradual sinking of the gauge. These years come before INA's series, which starts in 1884.
Not found: reading hours and readings per day, gauge moves, telemetry start, whether the gauge sinking affected years after 1883.

public_notes: Rosario's record in this file starts in 1884. Researchers describe Rosario's as the longest water level record on the Paraná; they corrected the earlier 1875 to 1883 readings, which are not in this file, for a slow sinking of the gauge.
